title: Your #6 is free: move away
brief: Your #6 receives facing your own goal with their #9 tight behind, so you come short to help.
briefKid: Your midfielder gets the ball facing our goal, with their striker close behind.
question: Your #6 has turned and is free, facing forward. Where do you go now?
questionKid: Your teammate has turned and is free. Where do you go now?

takeaway.standard: Come short while the carrier is in trouble, but once the carrier is free and facing forward, move 12-25 m away into the gap between their lines, where one pass breaks their midfield.
takeaway.kid: Teammate in trouble? Come close. Teammate free? Move away into space.

misconceptions.text: You stayed short next to your #6, but the #6 is free now, so you only crowd the ball and bring another opponent close to it.
misconceptions.textKid: You stayed too close. Your teammate is free now, so move away into space.

misconceptions.text: You ran out toward the touchline, where your winger already holds the width, so one opponent can cover you both.
misconceptions.textKid: That is your winger's space. Find the gap between their players instead.
